answer: An output-correlation detector resists sybil attacks by analyzing stylistic fingerprints of submitted work. Every identity must produce results across varied domains, such as a meadow restoration dataset, velvet fabric pricing, and reef survey scoring. Genuine agents develop distinct phrasing and quirks, while clones from one model show correlated outputs. Each epoch, clustering compares pairwise similarity; any group above a threshold is flagged. Running thousands of duplicates costs full compute per task yet risks detection, since hiding correlation across domains is nearly impossible.
